sources.title: ISO 18968:2026 listing (NORMSERVIS)
findings: Retailer lists ISO 18968:2026, release date 27.8.2026, 50 pages.
sources.limits: Retailer, not ISO; iso.org/standard/85512.html returned 403.
sources.revisit: check iso.org status page and BSI for final scope text

sources.title: ISO 18968 Shaping the Future of Translation-Oriented Writing (ATC ISO blog, draft stage)
findings: Standard guides writing and evaluating texts meant for translation, for humans or machines; criteria include terminology, syntax, formatting, semantic clarity.
Excludes fiction, journalism, advertising.
sources.limits: Written while the standard was a draft; clause text not seen.
sources.revisit: buy or preview the final standard before citing clauses

sources.title: ISO 24495-3:2026 Plain language - Part 3: Science writing
findings: Edition 1, 2026-05, status Published.
Builds on ISO 24495-1 and is organized by its four principles.
Science writing for readers with varying education levels; not journal articles. Applies to mostly text-and-image material, most written languages.
sources.limits: Scope abstract only; part 1 not opened.
sources.revisit: open ISO 24495-1:2023 abstract when iso.org is reachable

sources.title: ISO House Style (committee.iso.org mirror)
findings: Use plain language so readers can find, understand and use information; it reduces misunderstanding.
Documents have non-native readers and are often translated; clear concise writing avoids translation errors.
Short sentences and paragraphs, one idea per sentence, avoid sentences over 20 words.
"shall", "must", "need to" are not interchangeable; subtle differences do not translate.
sources.limits: Written for standards drafting; 20-word limit is a house rule, not a general law.

sources.title: DIN 5008 - Rules for writing and layout of word and information processing
findings: Edition 2020-03 is marked CURRENT; commentary publication 2020-06.
Beuth record of the 2011 edition (https://www.dinmedia.de/de/norm/din-5008/137578108) says it was replaced by DIN 5008:2020-03.
sources.limits: No project/draft list consulted; absence of a notice is not proof of no revision.
sources.revisit: check DIN project portal for E DIN 5008 each quarter

sources.title: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website
findings: Generating many pages with gen AI without adding user value may violate the scaled content abuse spam policy.
It is critical to manually fact-check and review all AI-generated content before publishing, including title, meta description, structured data, image alt text.
Models predict likely word sequences and may produce inaccurate output.
sources.limits: Not a ranking guarantee; page shows no visible date.

sources.title: Email sender guidelines (Gmail)
findings: Since 2024-02-01 all senders to Gmail need SPF or DKIM, valid forward/reverse DNS, TLS, RFC 5322 format; spam rate below 0.3%.
Senders above 5,000 messages/day to Gmail must support one-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed mail via List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click plus List-Unsubscribe.
Keep spam rate below 0.10% and never reach 0.30%.
sources.limits: Thresholds are per Gmail, counted per day to Gmail accounts; other mailbox providers differ.

sources.title: Email sender guidelines FAQ (Gmail)
findings: One-click unsubscribe is required only for marketing and promotional messages; transactional (password reset, reservation or form confirmations) is excluded.
Senders who already had an unsubscribe link had until 2024-06-01 to implement one-click.
From November 2025 Gmail ramps up enforcement; non-compliant traffic sees temporary and permanent rejections.
Unsubscribe link at top of message shows only for messages passing automated eligibility checks.
sources.limits: Promotional vs transactional is judged by recipients, not Google.

sources.title: RFC 8058 Signaling One-Click Functionality for List Email Headers
findings: Sender provides HTTPS POST endpoint from the List-Unsubscribe URI; it MUST NOT answer with an HTTPS redirect.
Message needs a valid authentication identifier (e.g. DKIM); URI should contain an opaque identifier; request must not carry cookies.
sources.limits: Protocol spec, not deliverability policy.

sources.title: DORA's software delivery performance metrics
findings: Throughput: change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time.
Instability: change fail rate and deployment rework rate (unplanned deployments caused by a production incident).
sources.limits: Page does not date the introduction of rework rate.

sources.title: DORA State of AI-assisted Software Development 2025
findings: AI's primary role is as an amplifier of existing organizational strengths and weaknesses.
Greatest returns come from the underlying organizational system, not the tools.
sources.limits: Landing page only; full report not read.

sources.title: DORA Report Finds AI Is an Amplifier ... But Trust Remains Low (InfoQ)
findings: AI adoption now correlates positively with delivery throughput, while delivery instability continues to rise.
Researchers tested whether speed offsets instability via fail-fast-fix-fast and found it did not.
sources.limits: Secondary summary; no verification/auditing-shift wording found.
sources.revisit: read primary report sections on review and batch size

sources.title: Writing good CL descriptions (Google eng-practices)
findings: CL description is a public record answering what changes and why.
First line is a short focused summary; body gives problem, why this approach, shortcomings, background links.
External links may become unreadable, so include enough context.
sources.limits: Google-internal CL culture; Gerrit-style review.

sources.title: Small CLs (Google eng-practices)
findings: Small CLs are reviewed more quickly and more thoroughly.
sources.limits: Practitioner guidance, no controlled study cited on the page.

sources.title: Pull requests (GitHub Docs)
findings: Pull requests let teams discuss and review changes before merging.
Conversation tab shows description, timeline, comments, reviews; separate tabs for commits, checks, files changed.
sources.limits: Product documentation.

sources.title: Conventional Commits 1.0.0
findings: Format <type>[scope]: <description> + optional body/footers.
Stated purpose: explicit commit history that is easier to build automated tools on; maps fix->PATCH, feat->MINOR, BREAKING CHANGE->MAJOR.
sources.limits: Does not say to use it only with automation.

sources.title: FaST Guide 2.1 (PDF)
findings: FAST = Fluid Scaling Technology, combining Open Space Technology and Open Allocation.
Optimised for design, discovery and delivery, not only delivery.
Work emerges in a Marketplace; Tribe Members self-select into teams.
Maps and Discovery Trees represent and make work visible.
sources.limits: Vendor-authored guide, 2021; no outcome evidence.
sources.revisit: Superseded for current terminology by FaST Guide v3.0 (SRC-WRITE-036), which uses Collective, not Tribe.

sources.title: FAST - Fluid Adaptive Scaling Technology (official site)
findings: Site expands the acronym as Fluid Adaptive Scaling Technology and describes self-organising around work, for delivery and discovery.
sources.limits: Marketing site, testimonials; conflicts with the guide's expansion.
sources.revisit: Superseded for current terminology by FaST Guide v3.0 (SRC-WRITE-036), which uses Collective, not Tribe.

sources.title: Professional Editorial Standards 2024
findings: Four editing stages from first iteration to last: structural, stylistic, copy editing, proofreading.
Part A fundamentals (2024 adds conscious language, accessibility); rewriting, indexing, localization out of scope.
sources.limits: English-language editing, Canadian body; definitions per stage not read (sub-pages not opened).

sources.title: GOV.UK A to Z style guide
findings: All GOV.UK content should be written in plain English with language the audience understands; "words to avoid" list exists.
sources.limits: UK English, government audience. The content design "writing for GOV.UK" URL only redirected and its target page was not opened.

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide - Highlights
findings: Conversational tone, active voice, second person, writing for accessibility and a global audience, descriptive link text.
sources.limits: Developer docs context.

sources.title: Write for a global audience (Google developer documentation style guide)
findings: Docs are written in US English with translation in mind.
Short unambiguous sentences, active voice, present tense, avoid colloquialisms, idioms, humor, seasonal references; keep terminology consistent.
sources.limits: Developer docs.

sources.title: Cross-references and linking (Google developer documentation style guide)
findings: Link text should make sense without surrounding text; do not use "click here" or "this document".
sources.limits: none

sources.title: Microsoft Writing Style Guide - brand voice (simple and human) and welcome
findings: Guide's voice principle is "above all, simple and human" (page title); detailed rules not extracted this session.
sources.limits: Only the voice and welcome pages were fetched (welcome: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/welcome/); thin evidence.
sources.revisit: extract bias-free communication and procedures pages

sources.title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide - Voice and Tone
findings: Voice stays constant, tone adapts to the situation.
Use active voice, avoid slang and jargon, write positively.
sources.limits: Company brand guide, not evidence of effect.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)
findings: Level A: users understand what each link does; provide descriptive link names or context.
Techniques accept link text alone or link text plus sentence or programmatic context.
sources.limits: Context-dependent: link text alone is not always required for conformance.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
findings: Level AA: headings and labels describe topic or purpose; helps orientation.
sources.limits: Does not require headings to exist or to be unique.

sources.title: git SubmittingPatches
findings: Describe changes in imperative mood, as if giving orders to the codebase.
Make the explanation understandable without external resources; summarize linked discussions instead of only linking.
sources.limits: Git project's own mailing-list workflow; git-commit man page (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit) opened but no subject-length rule extracted.

sources.title: Creating a pull request template for your repository (GitHub Docs)
findings: A PR template's contents appear automatically in the pull request body.
sources.limits: Location rules not extracted.

sources.title: Atlassian Design System - Content foundations
findings: Content foundations aim for clear, concise, consistent language in Atlassian apps.
sources.limits: Product UI copy guidance, not Confluence documentation guidance. No official Atlassian doc-writing guide found; community posts seen in search were not opened.
sources.revisit: look for Atlassian Team Playbook or Confluence docs guidance

sources.title: Shape Up chapter 13 Show Progress (hill charts)
findings: Hill chart: uphill = figuring things out, downhill = making it happen.
First third uphill = "I've thought about this", second = "approach validated", final = "no other unknowns believed".
Backsliding happens when uphill work was done "with the head instead of the hands".
sources.limits: Method from one company; no outcome data.

sources.title: Lesbarkeitsindex (German Wikipedia)
findings: Amstad adapted Flesch for German: FRE_de = 180 - ASL - 58.5 x ASW (ASL average sentence length, ASW average syllables per word).
Word length dominates in both Flesch indices, which limits applicability to German with many compounds.
Formulas measure two surface features directly and others only indirectly.
sources.limits: Encyclopedia, secondary; LIX article not separately opened.
sources.revisit: replace with Amstad 1978 and Bjornsson (LIX) primary sources

sources.title: Bottom line up front (Wikipedia)
findings: BLUF originates in US Army Regulation 25-50: main point first and active voice.
Resembles the journalistic inverted pyramid; deductive rather than inductive order.
sources.limits: Secondary; the AR itself and Minto's book not opened. Pyramid Principle primary not reached.

sources.title: Mayer's 12 Principles of Multimedia Learning (summary)
findings: Signaling: cues emphasizing key information and structure help learning (outline slide, arrows, bold).
Redundancy: graphics with narration beat graphics plus narration plus on-screen text.
Coherence: remove irrelevant material.
sources.limits: Practitioner summary of lab-based learning research, not a meta-analysis; about learning lessons, not marketing persuasion or hero animation. Signaling meta-analysis page (rex.libraries.wsu.edu) opened but only a title, no content.
sources.revisit: read Mayer 2009/2014 and the 2020 signaling meta-analysis in ETR&D 68(5)

sources.title: Duden Rechtschreibregeln
findings: Free reference of spelling and punctuation rules by number (e.g. D 100 to D 108 for comma in enumerations; D 5 to D 11 for quotation marks).
sources.limits: Rules index, not style advice; does not confirm the 2024 Regelwerk date.
sources.revisit: pair with Rat primary when reachable

sources.title: FaST Guide, Version 3.0
findings: Expands FaST as Fluid Scaling Technology.
The group of people working together is the Collective; everyone in it is a Member; a Collective can work on several products with several Product Managers.
Teams self-organize around work items in a Marketplace and record choices on a Marketplace Board; Discovery Trees break down work and track progress.
sources.limits: Read from a local PDF copy of v3.0 (January 2024); the web URL was not opened in this session. Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: cite, do not adapt.
